item: The article list's language filter and sort by title read only an index, built once at start-up as a task-manager job (R128)
key_paths: src/database/article_indexes.py; src/database/maintenance.py; src/database/models.py; src/database/session.py; src/api/boot_sequence.py; src/api/jobs.py; src/jobs/background.py; migrations/versions/c3a91f5e7b24_article_list_language_and_title_indexes.py; tests/test_article_indexes.py; tests/test_boot_sequence.py; docs/USER_MANUAL.md; src/api/main.py; src/scheduler/memguard.py; tests/test_vacuum_space_preflight.py; tests/test_perf_batch.py; src/api/database.py
summary: The maintainer answered 34a: both indexes. idx_article_language_published (language, published_at) and idx_article_title_nocase (title COLLATE NOCASE) turn the article list's two remaining slow shapes into index-only reads: the page query of a language filter 1,284 ms to 3 ms and of a sort by title 807 ms to 3 ms cold on a 40,000-article, 2 GB test library, the same answers in the same order. init_db leaves them out (maintenance.DEFERRED_INDEXES); an article-indexes step of the boot sequence, after the check of the data files and before the warm-up, builds what is missing as a task-manager job: one statement each under the write gate, 'index N of M', no Cancel (an opaque statement), the free space measured first (about 400 bytes an article on the database's volume) and the memory (the sort is held in RAM, about 300 bytes an article (measured 128 for Latin titles and 272 for Devanagari ones): declined below that plus the memory guard's floor; never a temporary file, because on an encrypted store the sorter's spill holds the titles in the clear, measured), a shortfall is a failed row whose keyed detail carries the numbers in both task managers and an unreadable figure is not a refusal, and a record of the attempt written before the first statement (two starts in a row that ended mid-build stop it until the app is updated; an orderly quit gives the attempt back), declined when the corpus file is paused as damaged, ANALYZE of just the new indexes afterwards. The title index is declared on the model with collate() so the stamp alignment reads no drift; the language one reads add_index for the one start before the step has built it. OO_ARTICLE_INDEXES=0 leaves them unbuilt. The diagnostics bundle's boot_sequence block carries what the step did. About 190 MB per 1.5 million articles on real titles (130 MB on the synthetic ones). The build on a big store on a slow drive is not measured: the bundle's block will say. The caveat reads anything the app saves waits (every gated write does), the in-app task manager draws the row's detail, a worker thread that cannot start leaves no phantom running job, and a second run carries nothing of the first in its snapshot. The report carries the process's peak memory before and after, labelled as the high-water mark. The Compact-database tool (POST /api/database/vacuum) is gated the same way, a new user-visible refusal: its rebuilt copy is held in memory, so it is refused with 507 and the numbers, before the write lock, when the memory available is below 1.25 times the pages in use plus the memory guard's floor, or the drive holds less than twice the pages in use plus the log; the copy is sized from what VACUUM copies (the pages in use, read on a connection, which counts what is still only in the log and not the free pages a delete left), the temporary volume nothing writes to is no longer measured, and a figure that could not be read is named in the detail and never a refusal.
